title: Control the planar high-mode quotient independently of first-mode forcing
statement: On the unit square torus let lambda1=(2pi)^2,E the ENTIRE planar first eigenspace,Q=||curl u||2^2-lambda1||u||2^2>=0,D=sum lambda_k(lambda_k-lambda1)|u_hat(k)|^2. For ANY time-dependent f in E with arbitrary amplitude/switching, 2D energy and enstrophy cancel both Euler and f: (1/2)Q_prime+nu D=<(-Delta-lambda1)u,h>. Spectral Cauchy-Schwarz gives Q_prime+nu D<=||h||2^2/nu,D>=2lambda1 Q. For ||h||LinfinityL2<=eta,Q(t)<=exp(-2nu lambda1t)Q(0)+eta^2/(2nu^2lambda1),nu integral D<=Q(0)+t eta^2/nu, and ||(I-P_E)u||H1^2<=3Q. Standard 2D H1 approximation gives the corresponding solution inequality. This extends high-mode control beyond V0 in E but has no low-E contraction or enhanced damping. In smooth3D the identity acquires integral omega.dot((omega.grad)u), with no sign/bound supplied; no 3D weak enstrophy identity or full common-force compiler is inferred.
